chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The apple radiates the stomach'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical benefit of eating apples according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the apple as 'nadhuh al-ma’ida,' a term interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating that the fruit radiates health or spreads beneficial properties throughout the stomach. This concise statement underscores the Prophetic tradition of viewing food as both sustenance and medicine, reinforcing the apple’s status as a staple of the Islamic diet for its digestive and restorative qualities.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ismail Bin Jabir who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The apple radiates the stomach’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ’Isma‘il ibn Jabir who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying,
The apple is a stomach cleanser.’”
